observations.enchanting: Inserted an unenchanted wooden pickaxe and three lapis. The first native offer displayed Efficiency I, required level 2, and cost one lapis/one level. Selection applied Efficiency I; ordinary-click extraction delivered the item. SDK close returned two unused lapis. Counts: three total pickaxes, two lapis; level 4 before to 3 after.
observations.permission_loss: Inserted another unenchanted pickaxe and two lapis. Temporarily de-opped the test player, revoking the example consumer permission. The native screen closed and returned its inputs; read-only counts stayed three pickaxes/two lapis. One failure callback was expected from this intentional denial. No ticket leaked. Restored the previous operator status and reopened successfully.
observations.native_x_close: After reopening, inserted an unenchanted pickaxe/two lapis and clicked the native X. Item counts remained unchanged and ticket retired.
observations.anvil_regression: Renamed the Efficiency I pickaxe to VCF Enchanted Pickaxe for one level, delivered with an ordinary click. The next crafting screen tooltip verified both the name and Efficiency I; count stayed three pickaxes and HUD level changed 3 to 2.
observations.craft_regression: Opened native 3x3 screen, inspected the renamed item, and closed with the SDK. No crafting ingredient transfer in this exact regression.
observations.alias: /etable opened the native enchanting screen and Escape closed its separate provider-owned ticket.
observations.form_regression: One SDK form action callback, zero outstanding form tickets.

counter_limit: The deliberate permission loss terminates with a failure event rather than a normal close. The provider-owned etable alias is outside the example counters. SDK events do not certify every native transaction.
not_qualified: Custom enchantment offers or plugin-owned item writes
earlier_anomalies: This run does not resolve ca30255 grindstone initial extraction rejection or the older 171e0aa missing-plank/death observation.
